transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Ava (CSM), Lena (EngageFlow Head of ML), Daniel (VP Eng), Priya (Sr DevOps), Omar (Security), Maya (PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick kickoff for onboarding EngageFlow onto Redwood Dedicated/Private options. Covered initial network topology, SSO/KMS requirements, pilot scope (30k daily requests), success metrics (p95 latency < 300ms, error rate < 0.5%), and immediate next steps (runbook, sample payloads, bench).

Topics:
- Network/VPC peering and egress
- Data residency & KMS
- Pilot sizing and SLA expectations
- Integration touchpoints (SDK, webhooks, tracing)

Action items (brief):
See action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Really appreciate it. Quick intros and we'll go into the runbook.
[00:15] Daniel Park: Hey all, Daniel here, VP Eng at EngageFlow. We're excited, we've got a bunch of use cases we want to move to production this quarter.
[00:22] Lena Wu: Hi, Lena — Head of ML. I'll be the day-to-day for model quality and evals.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Priya, DevOps. I'll handle networking and infra stuff.
[00:33] Sofia Patel: Great. Marco, do you want to kick off the technical bits?
[00:36] Marco Ruiz: Sure, thanks. So high-level, today's goals — agree pilot scope, network connectivity plan, and list blockers. We'll also review auth and encryption. I might go a bit deep on perf, hope that's okay.
[00:50] Maya Fleming: That's perfect. We need clear gating criteria.
[00:54] Marco Ruiz: Ok. First — ask: are you leaning hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC?
[01:04] Daniel Park: We're leaning Private (VPC) or Dedicated depending on latency. We have data residency constraints for EU customers, so VPC sounds better.
[01:12] Omar Hassan: From security: must have KMS for key management, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SSO via SAML. SOC 2 paperwork would be good to review.
[01:24] Sofia Patel: All doable — we'll share SOC2 attestation and our audit log guide. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via most major KMS providers, noted.
[01:36] Priya Nair: On networking — is there an option for private peering or do we need to open outbound egress?
[01:44] Marco Ruiz: For Private deployment we support VPC peering and transit gateway patterns; for Dedicated we can also do private connectivity. We'll send the network checklist but briefly: need CIDR ranges, any IP allowlist for your proxies, and if you use NAT or egress proxies.
[02:02] Priya Nair: Okay, we'll get CIDRs. Also curious about TLS — do you terminate on your side or do we manage certs?
[02:10] Marco Ruiz: We support mutual TLS for private links and can have customer certs in TLS termination. KMS ties into that as well.
[02:20] Lena Wu: On the model side — we want to pin a model version and have canaries for rollouts. How does Redwood handle model variant fallbacks?
[02:29] Marco Ruiz: You can pin versions in the deployment config and set rollback policies; we also do automated fallback to compatible variants if a GPU pool is constrained. Note: we'll need a small compatibility matrix from your side — e.g., sequence lengths and preferred quantization — but we can advise.
[02:46] Lena Wu: Got it. We'll send sequence length distribution.
[02:50] Daniel Park: Real quick on cost — what's the unit of billing for Dedicated vs Private? We want predictable monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go.
[02:59] Sofia Patel: Good Q. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; Private has license plus support for on-prem. We'll follow up with pricing sheet. For pilot we'll propose a short reserved window to get baseline.
[03:15] Maya Fleming: Success metrics: we want p95 latency under 300ms for 512-token average, error rate <0.5%, and token cost under X (we'll define).
[03:27] Marco Ruiz: Ok we'll attempt benching on your payloads. Can you share sample request shapes and typical tokenization? Small aside, sometimes request bodies have lots of preambles — prefix caching can help, we'll note that.
[03:40] Priya Nair: We'll provide sample payloads and a rate profile — bursts up to 600 r/s for short windows.
[03:47] Marco Ruiz: That helps a lot. For bursts we recommend autoscale + short-lived burst slots on Dedicated, or a hybrid routing policy if you want to offload to hosted for overflow. There's a tradeoff: latency vs cost.
[04:01] Daniel Park: Right, cost matters. We want low unit cost but not at expense of jitter.
[04:06] Marco Ruiz: Totally. Also, we've got continuous batching and KV cache tricks; depending on conversational vs single-shot calls, caching helps a ton. Quick note — sometimes transcripts say K-V case, sorry, our transcriber.
[04:19] (laughter)
[04:23] Ava Thompson: From CS side, we'll set up a weekly 30-minute sync for the next month.
[04:28] Sofia Patel: Sounds good. Next: timeline — pilot start target?
[04:32] Maya Fleming: We want pilot live in 3 weeks — so tentatively 2026-07-27 for an internal pilot.
[04:38] Sofia Patel: Ok we'll work backwards on network & benching. Two blockers to unblock before pilot: network peering and KMS/SSO config.
[04:48] Omar Hassan: We'll need a security deep dive — specifically around audit logs retention and key rotation policies. Also, data in tokens — does Redwood store request/response and for how long?
[04:59] Sofia Patel: By default we store request/response for 30 days for debugging; for Private we can set retention as you desire and offer no storage mode for regulated workloads. We'll include details in the security brief.
[05:12] Omar Hassan: Good. Also HIPAA-ish requirements for some EU customers, may need BAAs?
[05:18] Sofia Patel: We'll flag to legal; provide your compliance questionnaire and we can route it.
[05:24] Lena Wu: On instrumentation — do you expose opentelemetry traces or metrics endpoints? We want trace IDs correlated to our APM.
[05:33] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we support OpenTelemetry and you can inject trace IDs. We'll share sample agent configs. For token-level cost breakdown we can push to your metric sink.
[05:45] Priya Nair: About authentication — SAML for SSO and then token exchange for API calls?
[05:51] Sofia Patel: SAML/SCIM for RBAC and API keys for service-to-service. For Private we can also do mTLS and short-lived tokens signed by your KMS.
[06:02] Daniel Park: Any gotchas on install if we go on-prem? Disk, GPU drivers, container runtime?
[06:09] Marco Ruiz: For on-prem we need Nvidia drivers (if GPU), CUDA compat matrix we'll share. Also recommended container runtime and kernel tweaks for performance; the on-prem package includes a preflight checklist.
[06:22] Priya Nair: Can you share that preflight checklist?
[06:25] Marco Ruiz: Yes — action: I'll attach preflight + sample deployment YAML.
[06:30] Maya Fleming: On governance — who will be the internal stakeholders from EngageFlow?
[06:34] Daniel Park: I'll own exec sign-off, Lena will own model quality, Priya infra, Omar security, Maya PM for timelines.
[06:42] Sofia Patel: Perfect. Quick risk callouts: if pilot latency overshoots we can temporarily route to hosted for critical traffic; if token costs run high we can recommend quantized variants.
[06:53] Lena Wu: About quality regressions — we need eval harness to catch hallucination or regression. Does Redwood support eval hooks?
[07:01] Marco Ruiz: We integrate with evaluation pipelines; you can push test prompts and we'll alert on regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll show the Optimize tooling in the next session.
[07:12] Priya Nair: Ok let's talk schedule: what do you need from us this week?
[07:16] Sofia Patel: Immediate asks: sample payloads & rate profiles (Priya), CIDR and egress plan (Priya), KMS requirements and SAML metadata (Omar), and a compliance questionnaire (Omar). We'll send SOC2 and security brief by tomorrow. Marco will schedule the performance bench session for week of 7/13.
[07:36] Daniel Park: That sounds reasonable. How will we measure pilot success?
[07:39] Sofia Patel: We'll formalize a pilot success doc but tentatively — p95 latency <300ms, sustained throughput at X r/s with autoscale, quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval pass rate), and stable error rate <0.5%.
[07:53] Lena Wu: We'll feed back model evals weekly.
[07:57] Marco Ruiz: For benching I'll need a small test harness — prefer binaries or a script?
[08:01] Priya Nair: Script is fine, we can run in our CI.
[08:05] Marco Ruiz: Great, I'll prepare a load test script and a minimal client.
[08:09] Ava Thompson: I'll set weekly meeting invite and attach runbook when Sofia shares.
[08:13] Sofia Patel: Anything else?
[08:16] Maya Fleming: One last Q on data residency: can we pin EU data region for the pilot?
[08:21] Sofia Patel: Yes, we have EU-hosted regions or private VPC in EU. We'll include region options in the runbook.
[08:29] Daniel Park: Cool. If there are no more questions, let's recap next steps.
[08:33] Sofia Patel: Recap: Redwood will send runbook, SOC2 & security brief, preflight checklists, and load-test script. EngageFlow will provide sample payloads, CIDR ranges, and SAML/KMS metadata. Marco schedules perf bench week of 7/13. Weekly 30-min sync set by Ava.
[08:54] Omar Hassan: Thanks all.
[08:56] Lena Wu: Thanks.
[08:57] Sofia Patel: Thank you, talk soon.

End of transcript.
